title: GH#2: feat: statistics foundation: design, tables, collector and processor
body:
## Summary

First slice of Phase 1: the design, the tables, the collector and the processor.

- `docs/architecture.md` (design), `todo/PLANS.md` (phases; report engine and Overview come before the tracker; Phase 7 moves history from other statistics plugins), `AGENTS.md` rewritten as SEO Pro Stats's own guide.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`: six tables (dictionary, visits, pageviews, events, properties, daily summaries), made with `dbDelta()` on admin requests, dropped on uninstall.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collector.php`: WordPress-free collector. It checks host and Origin, limits size and skips excluded addresses (CIDR v4/v6). The visitor hash uses a daily salt, the IP is cut to /24 or /48, and the country comes from the CDN. Hits go to a guarded buffer file under a lock.
- `collect.php`: fast endpoint without WordPress, GitHub build only (`.distignore-wporg`); the WordPress.org build collects through REST. `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collection.php` handles the per-site folder and config, salts for today and tomorrow only, the hourly and minute cron, and a loopback test that chooses `collect.php` or the REST route `seoprostats/v1/collect`.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php`, `-ua.php`, `-channels.php`, `-dict.php`: turn buffer files into visits, pageviews, events and properties every minute: browser, OS and device; channel from referrer and UTM; country; 30-minute sessions; engagement and scroll; dictionary words in bulk. A resumed batch never counts twice. Bot hits are counted and dropped until the bots table (Phase 5).
- Core files synced from the starter (JavaScript build support, uninstall table check, Plugin Check handling of GitHub-only files: starter PRs 382, 384, 389).

For #2

## Runtime Testing

GitHub Actions jobs for this repository do not start (billing), so every check ran locally.

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker`: 0 errors. `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (WordPress 7.1.2, Plugin Check 2.1.0): WordPress.org zip 0 errors, 0 warnings. GitHub zip: only the expected updater and `collect.php` findings.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 and latest / PHP 8.3: pass. All six tables are made and none is left after uninstalling; no plugin queries on admin pages.
- Collector without WordPress: valid hits stored (204); wrong host or Origin 403; excluded v4/v6 not stored; 413 over 16 KB; 400 bad JSON.
- Preview site processor runs (comments below): visits, pageviews, events, properties and engagement stored, bots dropped, replays not counted twice, events without a path take their pageview's.

title: GH#2: feat: report engine, read REST API and WP-CLI
body:
## Summary

Second slice of Phase 1: the report engine, the read REST API and WP-CLI.

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php`: ranges in the site time zone (realtime, today, yesterday, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, week, month, year, 12mo, lastyear, all, custom). Comparison with the previous period or last year; a partial period meets a partial one. Filters `is`, `is_not`, `contains`, `matches` on 16 dimensions. Headline metrics, time series (hour, day, month), breakdowns, realtime. Each answer is cached for 5 minutes by request and data version; there is one entry per request, so entries do not pile up.
- Page and event queries bound the fact table by its own `ts` (`fact_window()`: the range's start to a day past its end, because a visit ends with its day when the visitor salt changes). MySQL then reads `pageviews` and `events` through `ts`/`path_ts`/`name_ts` instead of scanning them.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php`: `seoprostats/v1` `stats`, `timeseries`, `breakdown`, `realtime`, `markers` (empty until Phase 3). Reading needs `view_seoprostats`, mapped to `manage_options`. Responses keep WordPress's own no-cache headers for signed-in users; the engine caches on the server.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php`: `wp seoprostats stats|timeseries|breakdown|realtime|process|doctor`.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-dict.php`: read-only `find()` and `like()` lookups for filters.
- `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md` updated.

For #2

## Runtime Testing

Risk: medium (new read paths; no writes to visitor pages). Level: runtime-verified.

Local, because GitHub Actions do not start on this repository while it is private (billing; both `Lint (PHP 7.4)` and `SonarCloud analysis` show "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed", no steps ran). Head `6a2dccb`.

title: GH#2: feat: Overview screen, top-level menu and Dashboard widget
body:
For #2

## What

The first screen people see: an **SEO Pro Stats** top-level menu at position 3 (where site statistics usually sit) with an **Overview** of the site's traffic, and a **Dashboard widget**.

- `packages/core`: portable, WordPress-free and React-free types for the API contract, filters, URL state (`#/overview?range=7d&metric=pageviews&f=country:is:US`), metric definitions and number formatting.
- `packages/charts`: a uPlot timeseries chart (current period with the comparison period overlaid) and an SVG sparkline. No WordPress or React.
- `packages/wp-admin`: the React app on WordPress's own React and components (`@wordpress/element`, `@wordpress/components`, `@wordpress/api-fetch`), built into `assets/build/` (committed, as `DEVELOPMENT.md` requires). Overview: period and comparison controls, filter chips, metric tiles with change and sparklines, the main chart (with a table for screen readers), live visitors, and four cards with tabs: Sources (channels, sources, campaigns), Pages (top, entry, exit), Locations (countries, languages), Devices (devices, browsers, systems). Choosing a row filters the whole view.
- Widget: today so far against yesterday at the same time, the last 7 days' visitors, and a link to the Overview (38 KiB bundle).
- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php`: registers the menu (Overview, plus a Settings link to the existing Settings → SEO Pro Stats screen, which keeps its URL; the app has its own slug, `seoprostats-dashboard`), renders the screen and widget holders, and enqueues the built entries from their `.asset.php` dependency lists. WordPress before 6.6 has no `react-jsx-runtime` script, so a small inline stand-in maps it to WordPress's React.
- Reading needs `view_seoprostats` (administrators for now), the same capability as the REST API.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (Dashboard app), `todo/PLANS.md`, `README.md` (Where to find it), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Testing

Run locally in the worktree (GitHub Actions do not start on this repository while it is private, and Qlty is out of minutes: billing, not code; `AGENTS.md`).

- `npm run check` (TypeScript, strict): passes.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php js shell workflows phpcs phpstan build). Build: dashboard 108 KiB JS, widget 38.4 KiB JS (minified), React and WordPress packages external.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed. 10,001 posts seeded; every visitor and admin page 200 (including the Dashboard with the widget) with default settings and every feature on; queries ok; uninstall ok; no PHP messages in `debug.log`.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (WordPress 7.1.3, Plugin Check 2.1.0): no errors. WordPress.org zip: 0 errors, 0 warnings. GitHub zip: only the expected updater and `collect.php` findings.
- Preview site with seeded data (42,753 visits), in a browser:
  - All REST calls 200; the Overview and widget render; no errors from this plugin.
  - Keyboard: tabs follow the tabs pattern (one tab stop per card; arrows, Home, End; wraps). Metric tiles are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`).
  - Filters: choosing a row adds a filter chip and refetches with `filters[0]=country:is:US`. Removing the chip clears it. The period select refetches. The back button restores the previous view.
  - Accessibility tree: labelled period and comparison selects, a live region for realtime, a chart figure with a data table, tablist/tab/tabpanel, and row buttons read as "United States 1,468 Visits 36%".
  - Width 390 px: the controls stack, the tiles go to two columns, and the cards stay readable.
  - Admin colour schemes: the accent follows `--wp-admin-theme-color`. Tested by switching the body's scheme class, because a plugin on the preview site forces one scheme through `get_user_option_admin_color`.
- Found and ruled out on the preview site:
  - A `regeneratorRuntime is not defined` page error comes from another plugin's admin script. These bundles do not contain it.
  - A menu-management plugin there moves top-level menus into its own group. Without it, the menu sits at position 3.

title: GH#2: feat: tracker: pageviews, SPA, engagement, events, outbound links and downloads
body:
For #2

## What

The tracker: the browser script that sends hits to the collector, so the site records real traffic without a test seed.

- `packages/tracker` (`@seoprostats/tracker`): TypeScript with no dependencies, built with esbuild to `assets/build/tracker.js`, 4.9 KB minified and 2.5 KB gzipped (the architecture's budget is 4 KB). `npm run build` runs wp-scripts, then `build:tracker`. wp-scripts empties `assets/build/` first, so the order matters.
  - **Pageviews:** on load, on SPA navigation (`pushState`, `replaceState`, `popstate`) when the path or a kept parameter changes, and on back/forward from the page cache. Prerendered pages count only once they are shown.
  - **Engagement:** visible time and deepest scroll %, sent when the page is hidden or left, and only when they changed.
  - **Events:** `seoprostats('Name', {props, revenue})` (calls made before the script runs are queued by a head stub), `data-sps-event` / `data-sps-prop-*` attributes, outbound links and file downloads. Props follow the processor's limits: 30 at most, scalars only, 300 characters each.
  - **Privacy:** no cookies, `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`. A random ID per page load, kept in memory, joins a pageview to its engagement and events. Page addresses keep only UTM tags, the page-identifying WordPress parameters and owner-added ones. Ad click IDs are sent by name only (`gclid=1`) for the channel, never their values.
  - **Skips** localhost, `navigator.webdriver`, headless user agents and excluded paths, plus DNT/GPC when the owner switches it on (checked in the browser, so page caches keep one copy).
  - Hits use the existing `pv` / `eng` / `e` format (`SEOProStats_Processor`). They are batched within the collector's limits (25 hits / 15 KB per request against 50 / 16 KB) and sent with `sendBeacon` as `text/plain` (no CORS preflight), falling back to `fetch` with `keepalive`.
- `SEOProStats_Tracker` (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-tracker.php`) prints it inline in the footer via `wp_print_inline_script_tag()`, with its config in `data-cfg`. It loads only on front-end requests. Editors (`edit_posts`), feeds, previews, the customizer, embeds and excluded paths get nothing.
  - Filters: `seoprostats_track`, `seoprostats_tracker_skip_capability`, `seoprostats_tracker_config` (`q`, `dnt`, `x`, `h`, `u`), `seoprostats_page_props`, `seoprostats_tracker_inline` (false loads the file with `defer`, for a strict CSP). The tracking settings screen comes later in Phase 1 and will set these.
- **No query on visitor pages:** `SEOProStats_Collection::endpoint()` read `seoprostats_collector`, which has autoload off. The loopback test now also writes `seoprostats_endpoint` (`fast` / `rest`, autoloaded), and `endpoint()` reads that. Existing sites get it from the stored test result on the next admin request. It is deleted on uninstall. `SEOProStats_Collection::hosts()` gives the tracker the same allowed hosts as the collector.
- Docs: `README.md` (Tracking, for site owners and developers), `docs/architecture.md` (how it is printed), `todo/PLANS.md`, `changelog.txt`.
- Left out for now: hash routes. The processor drops the fragment from paths, so they need a processor change first; this is noted in the plan.

## Testing

Run locally in the worktree (GitHub Actions do not start on this repository while it is private: billing, not code; `AGENTS.md`).

- `npm run check` (TypeScript, strict): passes.
- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php js shell workflows phpcs phpstan build). The build check runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, so esbuild works without its install script, and a fresh build matches the committed `assets/build/`.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed. 10,001 posts seeded; every visitor and admin page answered 200 or the expected 404 with default settings and every feature on. **Every visitor page made 0 plugin queries** with the tracker printed. Queries ok, uninstall ok (no options, tables or cron events left), no PHP messages in `debug.log`.

title: GH#2: feat: daily summaries and retention; long ranges read the daily table
body:
For #2

## What

Daily summaries and retention (Phase 1 in `todo/PLANS.md`), so long ranges stay fast and old visits can be deleted without losing the record.

- **`SEOProStats_Rollup`** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php`), run by the minute job after the processor:
  - Summarises each finished site-local day into `daily`: one row for the site, and one per value of each of the 16 report dimensions (channel, source, UTM ×5, country, device, browser, OS, language, entry, exit, page, event). The numbers use the report engine's own SQL (`SEOProStats_Query::VISIT_METRICS`, visits by start time), so they match the fact tables.
  - A day is summarised an hour after it ends, and only once every hit received by then is processed. The processor now records `clear`: the time the last file it finished was taken. With nothing waiting, it is now.
  - A day's rows are replaced in one transaction, so a day can be rebuilt. The last summarised day is rebuilt once more with the next one, to pick up engagement that arrived late. The first run summarises every day since the first visit, oldest first, within the time budget.
  - **Retention:** once a day, after the summaries are up to date, it deletes visits, pageviews and their properties older than 13 months, and events and their properties older than 25 months. Deletes go in batches of 5,000 within the budget, measured back from site-local midnight. It never deletes from a day that is not summarised, and a pruned day is never summarised again. The `seoprostats_retention` filter sets the months (0 keeps forever) until the Settings task.
- **Report engine:** a range that starts at midnight reads `daily` for its whole summarised days and the fact tables for the rest (today, or the part of a day a comparison cuts), then adds them together.
  - Headline metrics and time series (day and month grains) use it with no filter, or with one `is` filter of one visit value.
  - Breakdowns use it with no filter. They add both parts per value in one `UNION ALL` query, so order and paging cover the whole range.
  - "All time" starts at the first day in `daily` or `sessions`.
- **Schema v2:** `daily.scroll`, the sum of a page's scroll depths, so page breakdowns keep average scroll as well as average time on page.
- **WP-CLI:**
  - `wp seoprostats rollup` summarises due days now; with `--from` and `--to` it rebuilds those days.
  - `wp seoprostats prune` deletes old rows now; `--dry-run` only counts them.
  - `doctor` checks that the summaries are up to date.
- `package-lock.json`: added the missing `packages/tracker` workspace entry (from #10). Without it, `npm ci` stopped the lint's build stage.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (processing, `daily` columns, retention, report engine), `README.md`, `todo/PLANS.md`.

## Checks

Local checks only: Actions do not run on this private repository (`AGENTS.md`).

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: results in a comment below.
- Preview site: summaries built from real data and checked against the fact tables. Results in a comment below.

title: GH#2: feat: settings: tracking, privacy, data retention and who sees the statistics
body:
For #2

## What

The statistics' settings (Phase 1 in `todo/PLANS.md`), replacing the filters that stood in for them. One feature, `SEOProStats_Statistics` (`includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php`), on three tabs of SEO Pro Stats → Settings:

- **Tracking**
  - **Collect statistics** (on): off prints no tracker. The collector config gets `off`, so pages cached with the tracker store nothing.
  - **Not counted when logged in:** roles, by default every role that can edit posts (as before). It replaces the `seoprostats_tracker_skip_capability` filter.
  - **Query parameters to keep:** the tracker's `q`.
  - **Other domains of this site**, with and without `www.`: they become collector hosts, and links to them are not outbound.
  - Under Troubleshooting: **Load the script as a file** (for a CSP without inline scripts), **Visitor address from** (CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-For) and **Visitor country from** (CloudFront, X-Country-Code, GeoIP module).
- **Privacy**
  - **Respect Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control** (off): the tracker's `dnt`.
  - **Leave out addresses and pages** (off): IP addresses or CIDR ranges for the collector, and path patterns for the tracker. Invalid lines are ignored.
- **Data**

The tracker is printed inline, so a cached page keeps the copy it was cached with. New SEOProStats_Page_Cache (includes/stats/class-seoprostats-page-cache.php) purges the page caches it knows, each through its own public function or hook and only when active: WP-Optimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, SiteGround Speed Optimizer, WP Engine, Breeze, Cache Enabler, Hummingbird, Nginx Helper and WP Fastest Cache. body:

title: GH#30: feat: purchases from WooCommerce, EDD, FluentCart and ThriveCart
body:
## Summary

Paid orders become one Purchase event each, with the order's total in its own currency, on the visit that placed it, so goals, funnels and properties count purchases and revenue with no setup.

- **WooCommerce** (classic and block checkout), **Easy Digital Downloads 3** and **FluentCart**: when the customer's own checkout request places the order (`woocommerce_checkout_order_processed`, `woocommerce_store_api_checkout_order_processed`, `edd_built_order`, `fluent_cart/order_created`), `SEOProStats_Purchases::current_visit()` works out the visitor hash as the collector does: same daily salt, address, user agent and host, and the same exclusions (collection off, excluded addresses and roles, DNT/GPC when respected). It keeps the hash in the order's meta with the time. When the order is paid, at once or later (`woocommerce_payment_complete`, `woocommerce_order_status_processing|completed`, `edd_complete_purchase`, `fluent_cart/order_paid`), one buffer line with that hash and the checkout time is written, so the processor joins it to the visit like any event. The meta is then replaced by a recorded mark, so each order counts once. Orders made in wp-admin, WP-CLI, cron (renewals) or an API have no checkout visit and are left out.
- **ThriveCart** (checkout on its own domain): once the secret word is saved under Settings → Tracking, the tracker config has `tc`, and a clicked `*.thrivecart.com` link gets the page load's random ID as `passthrough[spst]`. The account webhook (`/?rest_route=/seoprostats/v1/thrivecart`, which works with any permalink setting; GET/HEAD answer 200 for ThriveCart's address check) checks the secret word with `hash_equals` and takes `order.success`. Amounts are in cents, and test mode is skipped unless `seoprostats_thrivecart_test_orders` allows it. It finds the page load by its unique `pkey` and records the purchase on that visit. The last 500 order IDs are kept, autoload off, so a retried webhook counts once. Orders without a known page load are counted for `wp seoprostats doctor` and do not become visits.
- No order number, customer name, email or address is stored. Free orders are not purchases. Lines written on the server carry `s: 1`; the collector never sets it, and one without its own user agent (ThriveCart's) is not taken for a bot.
- Settings → Tracking → Record purchases (on by default) and ThriveCart secret word. Filter `seoprostats_purchase` changes or drops a purchase. `wp seoprostats doctor` lists the shops recorded. Uninstall removes the state option and both meta keys from each shop's order meta table.
- Also: `SEOProStats_Collection::cron_schedules` translates its label only after `init`. WooCommerce asks for cron schedules during `plugins_loaded`, which raised WordPress 6.7+'s "translation loaded too early" notice for seoprostats on every shop site.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` → Purchases, README.md, readme.txt FAQ, changelog.txt, todo/PLANS.md.

title: GH#34: feat: change log of posts, SEO fields, products, plugins and settings
body:
## Summary

A change log: what changed on the site, when and on which page. It is recorded as each change is saved, so traffic, rankings and sales can be set against the changes that moved them. The `markers` route, empty until now, is filled.

- **Recording** (`SEOProStats_Changes`, hooks only; nothing runs on visitor pages):
  - **Posts, pages and products** of any public post type: published (scheduled posts going live too), unpublished (draft, private, pending, bin, deleted), address changed, title changed, content edited (words added and removed, word count), internal links added, removed or reworded, and external sites gained or lost. A binned post is recorded at its address before the bin, not the `__trashed` slug.
  - **SEO fields** from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and The SEO Framework: SEO title, meta description, robots (noindex, nofollow) and canonical, from their post meta. A save that sets the same value records nothing.
  - **Products**: WooCommerce prices up and down, sales started and ended, out of stock and back (products and variations, through `woocommerce_before_*_object_save`). Easy Digital Downloads prices. Coupons published, changed and removed.
  - **Site**: plugins installed, updated, activated, deactivated and deleted. Themes switched and updated. WordPress updated. Search engine visibility, permalinks, site address and front page settings changed.
  - Each change keeps where it came from (`wordpress`, `cli`, `api`, `cron`) and, for people who edit the site, who made it. Customers are never named. Imports, autosaves, revisions and media are left out. Each change is kept once per request. The `seoprostats_record_change` filter changes or drops one.
- **Storage**: schema v6 adds the `changes` table (keys `ts`, `path_id,ts`, `kind,ts`). Changes are kept for good, outside retention. Demo data has its own table, and uninstall drops both. The tables update by themselves.
- **Reading**:
  - REST `GET /markers` lists a range's changes oldest first, for charts.
  - REST `GET /changes` lists them newest first, with `limit` and `offset`.
  - Both take `page` (that page's changes and the site-wide ones) and `kinds` (kinds or groups `content`, `seo`, `product`, `site`; unknown ones are refused with the list).
  - Each change has a one-line `label`, `path`, `old`, `new`, `meta`, `source` and `user` (the name only for `list_users` and WP-CLI).
  - WP-CLI: `wp seoprostats changes [--page] [--kind] [--range] [--limit] [--offset] [--format]`.
  - `docs/api/openapi.yaml` and `packages/core` types (`Marker`, `MarkersAnswer`, `ChangesAnswer`) are updated.
- **Demo data** adds a year of example changes: posts, SEO fields, prices, stock, coupons, plugin updates.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md` (Storage, Changes, interfaces), README.md, readme.txt FAQ, changelog.txt, todo/PLANS.md.

A Yoast description was set, then changed. Yoast noindex and Rank Math robots were set. Setting the same value again recorded nothing. title: GH#33: feat: attributed refunds and net purchase revenue
body:
## Summary

For #33. Implements the authorized refunds-only fallback; renewals remain on the issue because subscription extension payloads cannot all be verified and ThriveCart documents a different renewal event.

- Positive Refund events retain the original daily hash, timestamp, currency and properties. WooCommerce, EDD 3 and FluentCart refund hooks use confirmed installed contracts; ThriveCart uses refund.amount in cents and a stable webhook_id (event_id fallback).
- Purchase goal and property revenue subtract refunds per currency without counting them as purchase completions.
- Historical server-side refunds rejoin their original visit, not a later same-day visit; retained metadata never creates visits after retention.
- Legacy recorded marks without a visit cannot safely be refunded; unknown ThriveCart orders are ignored. Buffer failures and filtered-out purchases are not marked recorded.
- Connection-owned per-site database locks serialize paid/refund receipt checks, appends and mark updates. Receipts are evicted even when later ThriveCart orders are unjoined.

## Files and reference pattern

Changes follow the existing buffered purchase path in `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-purchases.php`, indexed reports in `class-seoprostats-conversions.php`, and visit grouping in `class-seoprostats-processor.php`. The processor integration was added to the canonical issue scope before editing because its latest-visit-only lookup could invent a visit for a historical refund. `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `README.md`, `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt` describe the metrics, privacy and limitations. No API response shape or portable package changes are needed for the refunds-only phase.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified. Local verification passed on exact pushed head `39f619d24aa4c21f77e121b692e7f1fba7e52442`, after refreshing the main branch. GitHub Actions are unavailable under the repository's documented billing limitation; local results are the verification evidence, not a claim that remote CI ran.

- `composer install`: passed (locked dependencies; PHP platform 7.4.33).
- `scripts/lint.sh`: passed PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS, PHPStan, TypeScript checks and reproducible build; no generated file drift.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: passed with 10,001 posts and 30,002 meta rows, indexed-query checks, no PHP messages, and clean uninstall.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: passed on latest WordPress/PHP 8.3 with the same query/log/uninstall checks.
- Disposable WordPress 7.1.3/PHP 8.3 with WooCommerce 11.1.2, EDD 3.7.1.1 and FluentCart 1.7.0: native refund creation/events verified. WooCommerce USD 100 purchase less USD 25 refund yields USD 75 in the campaign-filtered Purchase goal and source properties, with one completion. Explicit Refund properties remain positive USD 25.
- Historical refund after a later same-day visit, historical/live mixed batch, refund after retention, duplicate refund callback, unknown ThriveCart order, receipt expiry after unjoined orders, final filtered currency and positive per-currency amounts: passed.
- Six concurrent authenticated ThriveCart REST refund requests: one recorded, five duplicate responses, exactly one persisted EUR 7 refund. Incorrect webhook secret still returns 403.
- Independent closeout review: all four initial findings repaired and accepted. The reviewed PHP code is byte-identical after the main-branch refresh (`git diff 843382d HEAD --` the three PHP files is empty).

### Remote provider observations

The immediate exact-head observation found no executed code failure:

- CI Lint and SonarCloud have zero job steps. Both annotations say: "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased." Evidence: https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostats/actions/runs/37570072896/job/112626479603 and https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostats/actions/runs/37570072930/job/112626479710 . title: GH#43: feat: Google Search Console connection, final-day imports and undo
body:
## Summary

Adds the first outside data source: Google Search Console, through a service account, off until connected under the new Settings → Connections tab. Search clicks, impressions and positions by page and query are kept with the visits, so later reports can put search and traffic on one timeline.

- **Connections** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-connections.php`, new): one option, autoload off, with each source’s credentials encrypted (libsodium secretbox, random nonce, `v1:` prefix; key from `SEOPROSTATS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, else the site’s `AUTH_KEY`/`AUTH_SALT`), settings and job state. Connecting signs in and lists the readable properties before anything is stored; without a property, the site’s own is chosen (domain property first). Credentials are never returned.
- **Search Console source** (`includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php`, new): RS256 JWT sign-in for a one-hour token, property list, final-day detection (default `dataState`, so preliminary days are never imported), and per day four Search Analytics queries (page, query, page × query, device × country), paged at 25,000 rows.
- **Import job** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-import.php`, new): hourly while connected, never on a visitor page; 20-second budget and one lock per run. New final days first (asked at most every six hours), then the 16-month history back to the property’s first searched day, newest first, a minute apart. It signs in only when something is due. Paths go through the processor’s `split_url()` into the same `dict` rows as visits; other sites of a domain property are skipped; queries are dict kind 16; positions stored as position × impressions × 100. A day is replaced in one transaction by the primary key.
- **Imports and undo**: each run writes an `imports` row and its rows carry its id; undo deletes them by its days through the primary key. `reimport --from --to` brings days back.
- **Storage**: schema v7 adds `gsc_pages`, `gsc_queries`, `gsc_pairs`, `gsc_totals` and `imports` (indexes for page and query lookups). Retention: search data by page and query 25 months (Settings → Data, `seoprostats_retention` `search`), pruned daily; totals kept. `wp seoprostats prune` now prunes search data even before any day is summarised.
- **Interfaces**: REST `GET /connections`, `GET|POST|DELETE /connections/{source}`, `POST /connections/{source}/import`, `DELETE /imports/{id}` (settings administrators); WP-CLI `connect`, `disconnect [--delete-data]`, `search-console status|import|imports|undo|reimport`; `doctor` line; Connections tab with status, Import now, recent imports with Undo, change property/key, disconnect.
- **Uninstall** removes the connection option, job hooks, lock and tables.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md` (Search Console section, storage, retention, interfaces), `docs/api/openapi.yaml` (new routes and schemas), README.md, readme.txt (FAQ and External services for Google’s sign-in and Search Console API), changelog.txt, `todo/PLANS.md`.

Not in this PR: search reports in the dashboard, an OAuth client option, Bing Webmaster Tools (later children of #37).



## Files Changed

README.md, admin/js/seoprostats-connections.js, changelog.txt, docs/api/openapi.yaml, docs/architecture.md, includes/admin/class-seoprostats-connections-tab.php, includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php, includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-cli.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collection.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-connections.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search-import.php, includes/stats/sources/class-seoprostats-source-search-console.php, readme.txt, todo/PLANS.md, uninstall.php

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (latest WordPress, PHP 8.3) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: both passed. Visitor pages run no plugin queries, admin screens open, uninstall leaves no tables, debug.log clean.
- Throwaway Docker site (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3 and again on PHP 7.4) with a real service-account key mounted read-only; output printed counts only, never the key, account or property names:
  - **Not connected**: no job scheduled; doctor says not connected.
  - **Bad input**: text, a non-service-account JSON, an unreadable private key and an unreadable property each fail with their own message; nothing is stored. Without a property and no match for the site, the error offers the 28 readable properties.
  - **Connect (WP-CLI)**: option has the `v1:` ciphertext, no private key text, autoload off, and decrypts; hourly job and first run queued.
  - **First cron run**: imported 15–18 final days within the budget and queued the next run. Then the history was shortened to a week and `wp seoprostats search-console import` finished it; a second run added nothing, and an hourly run with nothing due made 0 HTTP requests.
  - **Rows**: every page row joins a path in the visits dictionary (all start with `/`, none with a fragment), every pair joins a query of kind 16, three device codes, 3-letter countries, newest day 3 days old (final data only), weighted position about 15.
  - **REST**: `GET /connections` returns no credentials; logged out is refused. `DELETE /imports/1` removed exactly that import’s rows and marked it undone; again deleted 0; an unknown id is 404. `reimport` of one day wrote a new import. Import now answered done; a bad property is 400 with Google’s message; an unknown source is 404.
  - **Retention**: an old page row was pruned and the old totals row kept; `prune --dry-run` and `prune` counted and deleted search rows.

No horizontal overflow (a phone overflow from the long service-account address was found and fixed); the only console error is the expected 400.

title: GH#62: feat: Bing Webmaster Tools as a second search engine
body:
## What

Bing Webmaster Tools as a second search engine. It connects with an API key, imports Bing's search data into the same `gsc_*` tables (engine 2), and adds an engine switch to Search → Rankings, Opportunities and Content. The REST API, WP-CLI and abilities all take an `engine` argument.

Resolves #62

## How Bing's data is stored

Bing's API answers whole periods, not single days:

| Request | Gives | Stored as |
|---|---|---|
| `GetRankAndTrafficStats` | site clicks and impressions by day (no position) | `gsc_totals`, one row a day, no device or country |
| `GetPageStats`, `GetQueryStats` | top pages and queries by week, with average position | `gsc_pages`, `gsc_queries` on the week's last day |
| `GetPageQueryStats` (per page) | one page's queries by week | `gsc_pairs` on the week's last day |

Two assumptions were checked against 16 months of a live site before relying on them:

- **Week alignment.** I compared the weekly bucket clicks (pages + queries) with the daily totals over each 7-day window, across 66 weeks. A bucket dated D matches the 7 days *before* D best (correlation 0.956, against 0.928 for "ending on D" and 0.83–0.92 for other shifts). So weeks are stored on D − 1. The newest bucket also rules out "starting on D" (21 clicks against 7 in the days after it).
- **Position scale.** `AvgImpressionPosition` holds real ranks (1–10 on the top queries, not ×10). `AvgClickPosition` is −1 (unknown), so it isn't used. A day's position is its week's position, weighted by impressions.

## Whole-week periods

Pages and queries only exist on week-end days, so a 30-day period can hold 5 weeks while the 30 days before it hold 4. That would create a false ~25% "decay". For Bing, `SEOProStats_Search::days()` widens the start of the period to the whole weeks its days fall in. Any 7k consecutive days hold exactly k weeks, so a period and its comparison always hold as many weeks. Widening rather than cutting keeps every chosen day with data: Bing's newest week ends up to 13 days ago, so "Last 30 days" would otherwise shrink to two weeks. Where widening would start before the first day with data (all time), the period is cut instead. Search, Opportunities and Content all use this. title: GH#73: feat: experiments, measured against unchanged pages
body:
Resolves #73
For #61

## What

Experiments, the first part of the SEO decision loop (`docs/seo-loop.md` → 1. Experiments): record a change and what it should do before the result is known, measure it against unchanged pages, and keep the decision with the numbers it was made on.

- **Data**: schema v8 adds `experiments` (keys `status_review`, `path_id`, `start`; kept for good). Each experiment writes a change of kind 81 `experiment` (group `note`) at its start, so it shows on the markers lane and in Changes; deleting the experiment deletes it. `SEOProStats_Changes::between()` reads a span's changes by key `ts`.
- **Measuring** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-experiments.php`): equal windows of 7–84 days before and after (the change day left out; Bing's weekly page rows from the week after), its pages against up to 200 unchanged pages (data in both windows, no change of their own in the span), the effect (ratio over the group's, or places for position), the group's 10th–90th percentile spread, minimum data, coverage, and confounders (search engine updates, site-wide changes, other changes to its pages). Suggests keep / revise / undo / inconclusive with reasons and a one-sentence summary that says "associated with" when there is no group. Cached like the reports.
- **Interfaces**: REST `GET/POST /experiments`, `GET/POST/DELETE /experiments/{id}` (read `view_seoprostats`, write `manage_options`); `wp seoprostats experiments list|add|show|decide|cancel|note|delete`; abilities `seoprostats/experiments` and `seoprostats/experiment-record`; OpenAPI contract.

title: GH#75: feat: decision queue (Search → Plan)
body:
Resolves #75
For #61

## What

The decision queue, the second part of the SEO decision loop (`docs/seo-loop.md` → 2. Decision queue): one ranked list of search work, made from the opportunities, that says what to do next and why.

- **Items** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-queue.php`): one per opportunity: `ctr` (rewrite a title and description), `missing` (answer a search the page lacks), `striking` (improve a page at positions 4–20) and `decay` (find why a page lost clicks, then update it). Each has its page and query, why it is listed, what to do, its figures and its score. Items are worked out from the cached Opportunities and Content reports when the list is read; only items someone acted on are stored.
- **Score**: potential clicks per 28 days × value × confidence ÷ effort, with every part returned. Value is the page's conversion rate of visits from search for a goal (smoothed toward the site's; `goal=`) against the site's, from 1 to 5. Confidence is the kind's own, less below 1,000 impressions per 28 days. Effort is the kind's unless someone sets another (1–5). The rules are in the response (`rules`).
- **Actions**: accept, done (starts an experiment on the page with the kind's measure; the item then shows the experiment's state), dismiss (hidden for 90 days), restore, effort and note. New items on a page with a running experiment are left out (`left_out`), so one change is measured at a time.
- **Data**: schema v9 adds `queue` (unique `ikey`; key `status_updated`); reads are by `ikey` or `status_updated` only.
- **Interfaces**: REST `GET /queue`, `POST /queue/{key}` (read `view_seoprostats`, write `manage_options`); `wp seoprostats queue list|accept|done|dismiss|restore|effort|note`; abilities `seoprostats/queue` and `seoprostats/queue-update`; OpenAPI contract.
- **Dashboard**: Search → Plan (`report=plan`, `status=` kept in the address): the ranked list with state and actions; choosing a score shows its parts, with effort and note (administrators).
- **Demo data**: one item accepted and one done (with its experiment).
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/seo-loop.md`, README, readme.txt, changelog, `todo/PLANS.md`.

## Verification

Checks run locally (Actions do not start on this private repository; `AGENTS.md`).

title: GH#76: feat: overlapping pages (Opportunities and the plan)
body:
Resolves #76
For #61

## What

Overlapping pages, the third part of the SEO decision loop (`docs/seo-loop.md` → 3. Overlapping pages): queries that two or more pages share, shown as candidates to review, not faults.

- **Opportunities kind `overlap`** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-opportunities.php`): queries where two or more pages each get at least 10% of the query's impressions (`rules.min_share`), with `rules.min_impressions` or more in all. Each row is the leading page's, with the query's totals; `pages` lists up to 5 pages with clicks, impressions, position and `share`; `leaders` names the leading page in each half of the period and `switched` says whether it changed; `potential` is the clicks the query would get if all its pages had the best of their CTRs. Rows with the most impressions outside the leading page come first.
- **Reads**: one grouped read of `gsc_pairs` by the primary key for the period (the 2,000 pairs with most impressions, as for `striking` and `missing`), plus one read by `query_day` for the first half of the shown rows. The second half is the period minus the first half. Bing halves are whole weeks.
- **Queue kind `overlap`** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-queue.php`): effort 3, confidence 0.4, metric clicks. Its potential clicks come from `potential`, and overlaps where no page does better are not items. The item sits on the leading page with every page in `figures.pages`. It is left out while any of those pages has an experiment running, and Done opens one experiment on all of them.
- **Interfaces**: REST and ability `kind=overlap`, `wp seoprostats opportunities overlap`, OpenAPI (`OpportunityOverlap`, `halves`, queue `figures.pages`/`switched`), and core types.
- **Dashboard**: a fifth Opportunities card, "Overlapping pages", with each page's share, position and clicks on the line after its link, and **Switched** with both leading pages. Search → Plan names the kind and explains its potential clicks.
- **Demo data** (`SEARCH_VERSION` 4): shared queries, plus one whose second page has led for the last 40 days. That query shows as switched on Google and Bing for 90 days and 12 months, and not for 30 days, because one page leads in both halves.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/seo-loop.md`, README (feature and changelog), readme.txt, `todo/PLANS.md`.

## Verification

Checks run locally because Actions do not start on this private repository (`AGENTS.md`).

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build; built assets committed).
- `npm run --silent typecheck` and `npm run --silent build`: passed.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --php 7.4` (WordPress latest): passed. `queries: ok` in both rounds, no PHP messages, and uninstall left no tables, options or cron events.
- `EXPLAIN` on the preview site's demo tables: the smoke test's admin pages do not call REST routes, and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is a core file from the starter, so the overlap reads were captured directly. Each was run for Google and Bing over 90 days, 30 days and 12 months (cut to 91 days). Period read: `type=range key=PRIMARY` (rows 90–2,730). Halves read: `type=range key=query_day` (rows 112–714). No full scans.

- REST as an administrator: `GET /opportunities?kind=overlap` returns 200 for Google and Bing, with `halves` and rows that match `OpportunityOverlap`. An unknown kind returns 400 `rest_invalid_param`, and a logged-out request returns 401.

title: GH#77: feat: content audit from WordPress (Search → Audit and the plan)
body:
Resolves #77
For #61

## What

The content audit, the fourth part of the SEO decision loop (`docs/seo-loop.md` → 4. Content audit from WordPress): facts about each published page, read from WordPress and the SEO plugin, judged with the page's search figures.

- **Page facts** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-audit.php`, schema v10 table `page_facts`): one row per page path with lengths, 8-byte title and description keys, H1 count, words, images and images without alt text, noindex, canonical elsewhere, and a `flags` bitmask. No text is stored.
- **When facts are read**: at the end of a request that saves, deletes or changes the SEO fields of a post (up to 50 posts; a bulk edit leaves the rest to cron), and by the daily cron, 200 posts within 20 seconds, from a cursor over WordPress's primary key. A page is read again when its post changes, every 30 days, or for every page when the SEO plugin changes. Unpublished or deleted posts lose their rows; a changed slug moves the row. Visitor pages do no audit work.
- **Findings**: noindex or canonical elsewhere (only on pages with impressions), thin (under 300 words, impressions but no clicks), title or description missing, long (60 / 160 characters) or the same as another page's, no H1 or several, images without alt text. Pages with most impressions come first.
- **Queue kind `audit`** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-queue.php`): one item per finding, with potential clicks from the page's expected CTR times the finding's share; effort 1 (thin 3, in `rules.audit_effort`), confidence 0.5.
- **Interfaces**: REST `GET /audit` (`finding`, `engine`, range and filters), ability `seoprostats/audit`, `wp seoprostats audit [list|run]`, OpenAPI (`/audit`, `Audit*` schemas, queue `finding` and `figures`), core types and URL state.
- **Dashboard**: Search → Audit with a finding filter, editor links, the facts behind each finding and pages that share a title or description; Search → Plan names audit items.
- **Demo data**: audit facts for the demo pages; removing demo data and uninstalling clear the audit's progress.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/seo-loop.md`, README (feature and changelog), readme.txt, `todo/PLANS.md`.

## Verification

Checks run locally because Actions do not start on this private repository (`AGENTS.md`).

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build; built assets committed). The webpack size warning for `dashboard.js` predates this PR (main's is already 248 KiB).
- `npm run --silent typecheck` and `npm run --silent build`: passed.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3): passed, `queries: ok` in both rounds, no PHP messages, uninstall left no tables, options or cron events.
- `scripts/demo-site.sh up --live-search` (disposable Docker site), WP-CLI:
  - `wp seoprostats audit --data=demo --range=90d`: 12 pages read, 9 with findings, one or more of each demo finding, most impressions first.
  - Live posts: saving two published posts and a draft wrote 2 rows; unpublishing removed one and republishing restored it; a slug change moved the row to the new path and back. A cron batch read 4 posts (`done: true`); a second batch read 0 of 4.

- REST as an administrator: `GET /audit` returns 200 for Google and Bing with `finding=title_duplicate`; an unknown finding returns 400 and a logged-out request 401. `GET /queue` lists 9 audit items with `why` text and `rules.audit_effort`.
- Dashboard on the demo site: Search → Audit (with and without a finding filter) and Search → Plan at 1,400 px, Audit at 390 px; no console errors.

title: GH#78: feat: internal links — orphans, converting pages with few links in, missing links (Search → Audit and the plan)
body:
Resolves #78
For #61

## What

Internal links, the fifth part of the SEO decision loop (`docs/seo-loop.md` → 5. Internal links): the links in each published page's text to the site's other pages, judged with search figures and conversions.

- **Storage** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`, schema v11): `page_links` (`(from_path, to_path)` primary key, key `to_path`, the first link's text as a dictionary id, and how many links) and `page_facts.links_in` (other pages linking in, key `links_in`), recounted for the pages whose links change.
- **Reading** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-links.php`, `class-seoprostats-audit.php`): links come from the same text as the audit's facts, on save and in the audit's daily batch, and a page's links are replaced each time it is read. Visitor pages do no link work. `SEOProStats_Changes::links()` now also returns per-target counts. Links to WordPress's folders, feeds and files are dropped; paths get the permalinks' trailing slash; queries are kept only with plain permalinks; at most 300 targets per page. An unpublished page, or one at an old address, loses its links. After the update every page is read again (`read` in the answer says how far that has got).
- **Lists**: `orphans` (no other page links in), most impressions first; `converting` (3 or more conversions of the goal from search, 2 or fewer pages linking in), most conversions first; `missing` (a page with at least max(10, days) impressions on a search does not link to the search's page with most clicks), from the 2,000 pairs with most impressions, as overlapping pages does. The front page is in neither of the first two lists, as menus link to it. Search targets do not exist yet (#81), so the "intended page" is the search's page with most clicks.
- **Queue kind `links`** (code 7, `class-seoprostats-queue.php`): one item per page and list (a missing link sits on the page to link to, with the linking page in `figures.link_from`). Potential clicks are the page's impressions (for a missing link, those of the linking page's searches) × the site's CTR at its position × 0.1 (missing 0.2, `rules.links_share`). Confidence 0.4, effort 1 (converting 2, `rules.links_effort`), done measures clicks.
- **Interfaces**: REST `GET /links` (`kind`, `goal`, `engine`, period, page filters, `limit`, `offset`), WP-CLI `wp seoprostats links [--kind] [--goal]`, ability `seoprostats/links`, OpenAPI (`/links`, `Links*` schemas, the queue's `links` kind, `finding` and `figures`), core types and URL state (`links`).
- **Dashboard**: Search → Audit gets an **Internal links** card under the findings, with a list switch that shows each list's count, a goal picker for converting pages, the pages linking in, and for missing links the searches with both pages' positions. Search → Plan names the items ("Internal links: Orphan pages") and explains their potential clicks.
- **Demo data** (`PAGE_LINKS`): two orphans (the update post and the FAQ), the pricing page converting with two links in, and three missing links.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/seo-loop.md`, README (feature, WP-CLI, abilities, changelog), readme.txt, `todo/PLANS.md`.

`scripts/smoke-test.sh` is unchanged: it is a starter core file (`scripts/core-files.txt`) and already EXPLAINs every plugin query from cron and page loads, including the link writes and recounts. The report's reads run over REST, so I EXPLAINed them on the demo site (below).

## Verification

Checks run locally because Actions do not start on this private repository (`AGENTS.md`).

- `composer install && scripts/lint.sh` on the final head: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build; built assets committed). The webpack size warning for `dashboard.js` predates this PR.
- `npm run --silent typecheck` and `npm run --silent build`: passed.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh --php 7.4` on the final head (WordPress 7.1.3, 10,001 seeded posts): passed, `queries: ok` in both rounds, no PHP messages; `page_links` was among the tables, and uninstall left no tables, options or cron events.
- `scripts/demo-site.sh up` (disposable Docker site), WP-CLI on demo data:
  - `wp seoprostats links --data=demo`: 12 of 12 pages read; orphans 2, converting 1, missing 3 (features → front page, rankings guide → update post, front page → privacy post), as designed.
  - 90 days: the front page was listed as converting with 1 link in. Fixed: it is now in neither list, and a fresh read lists 6.
- Live posts (the save path):
  - Two absolute and query-string links to one target merged into a single row (`links` 2); a file link and an external link were dropped.
  - An edit that pointed the link at the real address replaced the row, and the target's `links_in` went to 1. Unpublishing the source removed its links (`links_in` 0); republishing restored them.
  - A slug change on the source moved its links to the new path with no double count.
  - The live report's first read covered all 4 published pages and listed 3 orphans.
- Queue on demo data: 5 `links` items (converting /pricing/ 11.7, orphan update post 7.1, two missing links, orphan FAQ), with scores matching the formula. The features → front page item is left out because experiment 6 is running on `/`.
- REST as an administrator (application password): `GET /links?kind=missing` returns 200; `kind=nope` returns 400; logged out returns 401. Ability `seoprostats/links` run returns 200.
- EXPLAIN on the report's reads (demo tables): `page_facts` by `links_in`, `post_id`, `checked` and the primary key; `page_links` by `to_path` and the primary key. Fixed during checks: the missing-link lookups on `page_facts` and `page_links` now force the primary key, because on the small demo table the optimizer chose a `post_id > 0` range (every published page). The `gsc_pairs` read is the same top-2,000-pairs query as overlapping pages (#76).

title: GH#97: feat: shared reports — every tab as a section, data-led defaults, drag order, print chosen sections with every tab
body:
Resolves #97

## What

- **Settings → Shared reports can be filled in.** The fields were top-level settings, and a settings card only draws a switch or an options panel, so they showed titles with nothing to edit. They now sit in two panels:
  - **Agency branding** (switch, off by default): agency name, website, byline and an agency logo picked from the Media Library. Off: new reports carry only the site's own name and logo.
  - **Report colours**: accent swatches from the site's colours (the theme's editor palette first, then theme.json and Site Editor or Customizer colours; filter `seoprostats_share_palette`), an **Other colour** picker, and **Light or dark** (follow the reader's device, light or dark), which replaces the unclear "Report appearance".
  - The credit switch reads `Show “Statistics logged by SEO Pro Stats for WordPress”`, and so does the line on the report.
- **Share on every tab**, after the period and comparison dropdowns. With demo data it shows but cannot be pressed (it stays focusable and says why).
- **Every tab can be a section**: Overview, Search (once for each engine: Rankings, Opportunities, Audit and Content; never the Plan or Experiments), Goals, Funnels, Properties, Clicks and Changes, each once per report. The server checks each read's arguments against its normal route, keeps a Search section to its engine, and allows only page locks with Search or Changes (search data and the change log have no visits). Changes are a projection: kind, time, allowed page, a published page's title or a search update's name; never users, plugin or theme names, values or notes.
- **Share editor**: fieldsets (Sections, What readers can see, Branding) with even spacing; a missing name says so on Save; disabled controls say why; logos preview from the Media Library; branding starts from the Settings defaults. Reports can be edited from the list.
  - **A new report starts with every section that has live data**, the tab on screen first (`GET /shares` now returns `sections`, from `SEOProStats_Shares::sections_with_data()`: one-row reads of each live table and the stored goals and funnels).
  - **Sections are reordered by dragging their handle** (mouse, pen or touch), or with the keyboard: Tab to the handle, Space, arrows or Home/End, Space to drop, Escape to cancel; each move is announced. Only sections not yet added are offered.
- **The private link** shows in a success notice with the full address, **Copy link** and **Open** (new window).
- **The reader's report**: header with logo, title and section, Light/Dark and Print buttons (no ring after a click; the keyboard keeps one), dark fields and notices that read well, and no owner hints ("an administrator can…", settings paths) or "By" column.
  - **The accent stays the brand's hue in both modes**: a colour too light for the white page is darkened (or too dark for the dark page lightened) in small steps until text reaches 4.5:1, instead of falling back to WordPress blue. Example: `#f5c400` reads as `#876c00` on light and stays `#f5c400` on dark.
  - Breakdowns a report hides (site search terms, referrers, UTM terms) show no tab (`hidden_dimensions` in the open response), rather than an empty one.
- **Print or save as PDF** (and Ctrl/Cmd+P) first asks which sections to print, all ticked. Each chosen section then prints with **every tab** (every Overview breakdown tab, every Search list for its engine, every Clicks list), starting a new page, for the period on screen. Printing waits for the data, is light whatever the screen, fits charts to the page, lists the period's changes by date, and keeps short tabs whole while long tables break between rows.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostats-statistics.php`, `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-share-settings.php` (new), `includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php`, `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-dashboard.php`: settings panels, palette, Media Library on the dashboard.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-shares.php`: sections, Search engines and reports, uniqueness, page-only locks, `sections_with_data()`, `SENSITIVE_DIMENSIONS`.

title: GH#68: feat: Combined search engine on Rankings, Opportunities and Content
body:
## Summary

Adds **Combined** (`engine=all`) to Search → Rankings, Opportunities and Content in wp-admin, the REST API, WP-CLI (`--engine=all`) and the abilities. Combined adds up every engine with data:

- Clicks, impressions and `pos_impr` are summed, so CTR and impression-weighted position cover all engines. A query or page that appears on more than one engine shows as one row, because they share one dictionary id.
- The period ends at the earliest of the engines' newest days (`SEOProStats_Search::span()`), so a lagging engine never looks like a drop. When any engine is weekly (Bing), the period is whole weeks. Each daily day is added to the week it falls in, and the weeks end on the period's last day.
- Combined has no countries or devices.
- `all` is not a stored engine code. Reads use `engine IN (…)` (`engine_where()`); each engine is still a range of the primary key `(engine, day, …)` or of the `path_day`/`query_day` keys named in `FORCE INDEX`.
- While fewer than two engines have data, `all` answers as the one engine with data (`report_engine()`). The answer's `engine` says which. A new `combined` boolean in the search, opportunities and content answers says whether Combined adds anything up. The dashboard offers the Combined button only when it does, or when Combined is already chosen.
- The default is still `google`. Audit, Targets, Plan and Experiments read one engine: Google when Combined is chosen (`singleEngine()` in core). Shared reports keep one engine per Search section, and `shareView()` drops `all`.

Docs: OpenAPI (`combinedEngine` parameter on /search, /opportunities and /content; `SearchEngine` enum; `SearchCombined`), architecture, README, readme.txt and changelog.

title: GH#109: feat: Settings → Import from Burst Statistics, with overlap rules and leftover cleanup
body:
## Summary

Settings → Import brings another statistics plugin's history across, starting with Burst Statistics (read from version 3.7.2), and removes what the old plugin left behind once it is switched off. This is the first child of #108: the engine, the tab, cleanup and the first adapter.

- **Engine** (`SEOProStats_Migrate`, `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-migrate.php`): adapter registry plus the `seoprostats_migrate_sources` filter. Detection is based on the plugin's data and cached for ten minutes. Dry run, overlap and `prefer`, a job in 20-second budgets under a lock (WP-Cron, plus the tab's polling; WP-CLI runs to the end), one transaction per day, undo in batches by primary key, the check against the source's own totals, settings filled in only where ours are still at their default, and a timeline note.
- **Imported days** live in `daily` with `import_id` (schema v15). Only days before our own first day are imported, and never a day another import filled, so a second run adds 0. The rollup deletes and rewrites only `import_id = 0`.
- **Adapter base** `SEOProStats_Migrate_Source` and **Burst** `SEOProStats_Migrate_Burst` read counts and names only. No IP addresses, visitor IDs or user agents are read. A bounce is a visit of one pageview, as we count it; Burst's own `bounce` flag starts at 1 and is cleared later by its cron, so it is not read.
- **Cleanup** deletes exactly the adapter's `leftovers()` list (tables, options, transients, cron hooks, user meta, files) after confirmation. It is refused while the plugin is active on the site or network, and needs `delete_plugins` and `manage_options`. On multisite it acts on this site only. The `AGENTS.md` rule records this exception.
- **Interfaces**: Import tab plus `admin/js/seoprostats-import.js`; REST `GET /migrate`, `POST /migrate/{source}`, `POST /migrate/{source}/cleanup`, and `DELETE /imports/{id}` routed by source; `wp seoprostats migrate list|run|imports|undo|cleanup`; abilities `seoprostats/migrate` and `seoprostats/migrate-import` (cleanup is for people only); `uninstall.php` clears the job, the cache and the cron hook.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (new section "Moving from other statistics plugins", plus `daily.import_id`), `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `README.md`, `readme.txt` (two FAQs), `changelog.txt`.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High (new schema column, writes to `daily`, drops another plugin's tables on confirmation)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified. Checks ran locally because Actions do not start on this private repository (billing).
  - `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build). `npm run typecheck` passed.
  - `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4` both passed: every page 200, the plugin's queries pass EXPLAIN, no PHP messages in debug.log, clean uninstall. `php -l` on PHP 7.4 passed for every changed PHP file; PHPCS (PHPCompatibilityWP, `testVersion` 7.4-) and PHPStan (`phpVersion` 70400) cover 7.4 too. On this PR, Actions and qlty did not start (billing or out of minutes), not because of code.
  - Disposable Docker site with Burst Statistics 3.7.2, front-end traffic, and Burst rows copied to the 5 days before our first day:
    - The dry run listed 5 days (1 skipped as our own) and the rows per report, and wrote nothing.
    - The import added 5 days and 165 rows, and the check matched Burst exactly (90/90 pageviews, 45/45 visits, 45/45 visitors). Pages, channels and the timeline note showed in the reports.
    - Running it again added nothing ("5 already imported"). Undo deleted exactly 165 rows and the note, and re-importing worked.
    - With Burst's Do Not Track, roles and IP block list set, those settings were filled in; ours were at their default.
    - `wp seoprostats rollup` over the imported days left all 165 imported rows.
  - **Overlap**: two throwaway adapters on the test site only (data present, plugin not installed, shown as "Deleted, data left"):
    - The dry run showed the 4 shared days and suggested the source with more pageviews.
    - `--prefer` with the other source let it fill the shared days first. The second filled only the days left, and days the Burst import had filled were skipped. No day ended up with rows from two imports.
  - **Cleanup**:
    - Refused with 409 while Burst was active (REST and CLI); an unknown source returned 404.
    - After deactivating Burst, the list showed 20 tables, 23 options, 4 transients, `uploads/burst/` and its must-use plugin. The UI removal deleted exactly those.
    - The site's other 54 tables and its other options were untouched, the 165 imported rows stayed, a timeline note was added, and detection no longer listed Burst.
  - EXPLAIN of the migration's own queries: our first day and the undo delete use the `daily` primary key, filled days use `dim_val_day`, imported-through uses `source_status`, and the owners lookup is a const lookup.

  - Also fixed during testing: the Burst adapter used the processor before it was loaded (fatal error in the dry run), and the dry run counted visitors once over the whole range while the check summed each day's visitors. Both now count each day's visitors.

`scripts/smoke-queries.php` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` are starter core files, so the migration's index checks were run by hand above instead of being added there.

title: GH#110: feat: moving notices from import to removal, on Plugins and SEO Pro Stats screens
body:
## Summary

One clear next step for each other statistics plugin found, from finding its data until the plugin and its data are gone, with SEO Pro Stats counting the whole time. This is the notices child of #108.

- **New** `SEOProStats_Migrate_Notices` (`includes/admin/class-seoprostats-migrate-notices.php`), loaded in `admin()`. The states follow the issue:
  - `import`: days not imported yet. Links to the Import tab at the plugin's card.
  - `check`: nothing to import and it still records. Check the import and Deactivate, or the adapter's `removal_step()`; its delete-data setting is named when it has one.
  - `remove`: inactive, or deleted with data left. Delete (core's delete-selected flow, single sites) and Remove leftover data.
  - none: nothing shown.
- **Where**, for people who can `activate_plugins`: a top notice and a row note on the Plugins screen (core's update-note markup, joined to the row), and the top notice on SEO Pro Stats's own screens except the Import tab.
- **Hide** is per person per `slug:state` (user meta `seoprostats_migrate_notices_hidden`, nonce'd `admin-post`). A plugin shows again when its step changes.
- **Screens never read other plugins' tables.** `SEOProStats_Migrate::found()` now saves the facts the notices need (option `seoprostats_migrate_notices`, autoload off, including the days still to import from `make_plan()`); the notices add only whether the plugin is installed and active. Plugins activated, deactivated or deleted, and a list over a day old, schedule a background look (`seoprostats_migrate_scan`, plus a daily check on the hourly hook); a finished import, an undo and a cleanup look again at once. `found()` also pins the live schema set.
- `SEOProStats_Migrate_Source` gains an optional `removal_step()` for plugins that do other jobs (Jetpack, #111).
- No statistics plugin is added to any `replaces` list. `uninstall.php` clears the option, the scan hook and the hidden-step user meta.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (notices table and rules), `README.md`, `readme.txt` FAQ, `changelog.txt`.

## Files Changed

README.md, changelog.txt, docs/architecture.md, includes/admin/class-seoprostats-migrate-notices.php, includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collection.php, includes/stats/class-seoprostats-migrate.php, includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-source.php, readme.txt, uninstall.php

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (admin notices and an option; no schema change; deleting data stays in the existing confirmed cleanup)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified. Checks ran locally because Actions do not start on this private repository (billing).
  - `composer install && scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build).
  - `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passed on WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.3 and on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4: every page 200, the plugin's queries pass EXPLAIN, no PHP messages, clean uninstall. Visitor pages run none of the plugin's queries; the Burst detection queries ran only in the cron run.
  - Disposable Docker site with Burst Statistics 3.7.2 and 6 days of Burst data (5 before SEO Pro Stats's first day). Every state was checked in WP-CLI and in the browser (Playwright, 1280×900 viewport screenshots, no console errors):
    1. Active with history: top notice and row note in `import`. The link lands on the Import tab at `#spst-import-burst-statistics`, with no notice there.
    2. After import (30/30 pageviews, 15/15 visits): `check`, with Check the import and Deactivate, without a manual rescan.
    3. Clicking Deactivate in the notice: core deactivates, and the page shows `remove` (Delete, Remove leftover data).
    4. Plugin deleted, data left: the top notice shows `remove` with only Remove leftover data, and there is no row.
    5. After Remove leftover data: no notice, without a manual rescan.
  - Activation, deactivation and deletion each queued `seoprostats_migrate_scan`.
  - Hide removed the top notice for that person and step only. A bad nonce got 403, and the hidden `check` step did not hide the later `remove` step.
  - A query watcher on admin requests logged no migrate queries on the Plugins and SEO Pro Stats screens. Only the Import tab reads the cached list and our own tables, as before.
  - With Burst active, no setting reported a replaced plugin, and both trackers printed on the page.
  - Found and fixed during testing: the notices stayed stale for up to a day after an import, undo or cleanup (`forget_found()` now looks again at once), and Hide dropped keys longer than 20 characters (now up to 100).

## Decisions

- The row note under the plugin always shows its step, as core's update notes and `SEOProStats_Replaced_Plugins` do; Hide applies to the top notice.
- The notices load the migrate classes only for a plugin past its import step, to ask the adapter for its stop step, without a query.
- The Delete link uses core's delete-selected flow, so the plugin's own uninstall runs. It is left out on multisite, where deleting is a network action.

body:
## What

Settings → Import now reads **Slimstat** (`slimstat`, from 5.5.0) and **Matomo for WordPress** (`matomo`, from 5.13.1, Matomo 5.13). Both keep raw rows, often millions, so this PR also adds a fast dry run for large sources.

- **Slimstat** (`includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-slimstat.php`): reads `slim_stats` and `slim_stats_archive` (its Archive Mode) with grouped queries per day on the `dt` index. `dt` is WordPress's legacy local timestamp, so a site day is `dt`'s UTC day. Crawlers (`browser_type` 1) and wp-admin pageviews are left out. Each `visit_id` is a visit (rows without one are a visit each) and each visit counts as one visitor. Also reads bounces, time on page to `dt_out` (at most 30 minutes), pages, entry and exit pages, sources, channels, campaign tags, search landings, countries, devices, browsers and systems.
- **Matomo for WordPress** (`…-matomo.php`): reads the raw `log_visit`, `log_link_visit_action` and `log_action` tables. It does not use the reporting API, which loads only while Matomo is active, boots all of Matomo inside the request and starts archiving. Archive blobs are not decoded. Visits are filed by their last action's time (UTC), as Matomo files them, with pageviews from their page actions. Also reads visit time and time on page, with the campaign name and keyword as `utm_campaign`/`utm_term`. Its browser, system and device codes become names. The IP, visitor ID, config ID and user agent columns are never selected.

The response sets `estimated`, and the CLI and the Import tab say so. The check after import still uses exact counts.

title: GH#111: feat: Settings → Import from Jetpack Stats (WordPress.com, built from Jetpack's source)
body:
## What

Settings → Import now reads **Jetpack Stats** (`jetpack`): the full Jetpack plugin or the standalone Jetpack Stats plugin. It was built from Jetpack 16.3's open-source code (stats package 0.22.1) and the WordPress.com Stats screens' source, without a connected test site, as the owner decided. People who use Jetpack test it.

Unlike the other sources, Jetpack keeps its history on WordPress.com, so this is the first remote source:

- **Adapter** (`includes/stats/migrate/class-seoprostats-migrate-jetpack.php`): its docblock cites each endpoint, parameter and answer field from the source. It reads only while Jetpack is active, connected, and has Stats on, using Jetpack's own two checks. Requests go through Jetpack's connection client as the site (`wpcom_json_api_request_as_blog`, API 1.1, 20 s timeout). They skip Jetpack's `fetch_stats()`, which would leave a `jetpack_restapi_stats_cache_` transient for every day of history.
- **Daily views and visitors**: `stats/visits` is read 90 days per request, back to the first day with views; the lookup stops after 180 days without any. The results are kept as counts in the `seoprostats_migrate_jetpack` option and refreshed daily. The lookup steps back correctly whether a window ends on its `date` or starts on it.
- **Per day**: the top 100 posts and pages (by current address; posts deleted since are left out), referrers (hosts and channels) and countries.
- **Only in cron and WP-CLI**: no requests on visitor pages, screen loads or REST.
- **Remote sources in the job**: an adapter's `days()` may return a `WP_Error` with `retry` seconds. The job puts the day back and waits longer after each try. It stops that plugin's import after six tries, or at once when trying again cannot help. The running job's queue items gain `notice` and `wait`, which the Import tab shows while it waits.
- **`unavailable()`** (new adapter method) says why a plugin in use cannot be imported now: connect Jetpack, update Jetpack, or its history is still being looked up. It appears on the Import tab (where the Import button is held back), in `wp seoprostats migrate list`, in `sources[].unavailable`, and as the dry run's and import's 409 error. The moving notices wait meanwhile.
- **`wp seoprostats migrate run --requests`** lists the adapter's requests for problem reports: path, HTTP code, error code, the answer's keys, list counts and first/last day. It never shows tokens or statistics, and it also prints when the run fails. The flag is not `--debug`, because WP-CLI keeps that for itself and never passes it to commands.
- **Settings**: Jetpack's `count_roles` fill our skipped roles where ours are still at the default.
- **Removal step**: switch off Stats in Jetpack, or deactivate the standalone plugin. Remove leftover data lists only its statistics caches, never its connection, modules or other options.
- **Fix**: `SEOProStats_API::with_status()` added error data even when nothing changed, so REST errors carried a duplicate `additional_data`.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml` (`MigrateJob` notice/wait, `MigrateStatus` unavailable), `README.md`, `readme.txt` (FAQ: how to report), `changelog.txt`, `todo/PLANS.md` (follow-up: testing on connected sites) and the WP-CLI help.
- PHPStan: local adapters' `days()` docblocks are narrowed, so they do not inherit the remote `WP_Error`. `phpstan-plugin.neon` ignores the Jetpack classes, which are not in the analysis.

## Verification

- Disposable WordPress with Jetpack 16.3 installed from wordpress.org, active but not connected:
  - `migrate list` shows the note "Connect Jetpack to WordPress.com first".

title: GH#131: Import: clearer settings table, with a checkbox per setting to carry over
body:
## What

Settings → Import's settings table is easier to read, with a checkbox per setting to carry over (Resolves #131).

- **Layout**: one row per setting. A checkbox column, the SEO Pro Stats setting in bold with the other plugin's own name for it below, then the plugin's value, ours now and ours after the import. Cells align to the top; long values wrap. On a phone the table scrolls sideways in its box, like the other Import tables.
- **Choosing**: a setting the import would change is ticked by default. Unticking it changes its "After the import" cell to "Stays: …". A setting that is already the same, or that you changed from the default, is disabled and says why. When there are no days to import, the table shows without checkboxes (settings are carried over with an import).
- **Role names**: excluded roles show as names (Administrator, Editor), not slugs. This uses a shared `SEOProStats_Migrate_Source::role_names()` helper in the Burst, Koko, Matomo, WP Statistics and Jetpack adapters.
- **Contract**: `POST /migrate/{source}` and the `seoprostats/migrate-import` ability take `settings` (keys from the dry run; `[]` carries none; without it, every setting the dry run would change, as before). `wp seoprostats migrate run` takes `--settings=<keys>|none`. The job keeps the choice, and `finish()` applies only those keys; a key's related settings follow it (Koko's IP addresses turn on exclusions).

- **Blocks**: `seoprostats/ab-test` (testId, name, status draft|running|paused|ended, goals, winner) holds 2–10 `seoprostats/ab-variant` blocks (slug, label, weight 0–100), each holding any blocks. Both are registered in PHP with render callbacks.
- **Editor** (`packages/wp-admin/src/ab-test/`, its own `ab-test` webpack entry): an A/B test button in the block toolbar and the More menu wraps the selected block or blocks. Variant A holds them, and Variant B starts as a copy. A variant dropdown in the test's toolbar picks the variant shown in the canvas. The sidebar edits the name (the post title by default), status, goals (from Goals), and each variant's label, weight and order. It also adds variants (blank or a copy) and removes them. In the site editor, template parts and synced patterns, the button only says that tests start in posts and pages for now.
- **Registry**: `wp_insert_post_data` renews a test id that is missing or used elsewhere, in this post or another. It rewrites only that test's opening comment, and saving again gives the same id. `save_post` upserts the post's tests into `ab_tests` (schema v16; primary key `test_id`, keys `post_id` and `status`). Tests taken out of a post, or in a deleted post, are marked `removed`, not deleted. Auto-drafts are skipped. This runs only when a post is saved.
- **On the site**: the control (Variant A, or the winner) is normal markup. A running test on a front-end page also prints its other variants in `<template>`s with an inline script under 1 KB. Feeds, embeds, REST and wp-admin get the control only (filter `seoprostats_ab_tests_swap`). The script picks a variant by weight before paint and swaps it in. It sets `data-spst-ab="<test>:<variant>"` for #134. It makes no query, option read, remote request, cookie or browser storage. Draft, paused and ended tests print only the control or winner.
