title: GH#134: A/B tests 2/4: exposures by page load, clicks per variant, opt-in one variant per visit
body:
## Summary

Part 2 of #29: record which A/B test variant each page load showed, privately, and count clicks inside each variant. Reports (#135) and results and the winner in the editor (#136) follow. Part 1 was #133 (PR #137).

- **Tracker** (`packages/tracker/src/index.ts`): a pageview sends `ab`, up to 20 `test:variant` pairs read from the page's `data-spst-ab` wrappers, which the swap script sets before the deferred tracker runs. A click inside a variant sends that variant's pair. The compressed size goes from 3,739 to 3,815 bytes (+76), still under 4 KB.
- **Processor** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php`): checks each pair's format (a test is 6–32 lower-case letters and digits; a slug is `a-z0-9-`, up to 64 characters) and keeps the first pair for each test. It then keeps only tests and variants listed in `ab_tests`, using one primary-key query per batch, so a forged hit cannot add tests, variants or dictionary text. It writes `ab_exposures` with `INSERT IGNORE`, so a resumed batch adds nothing, then adds the batch's clicks inside each variant to that page load's row. A click that claims a variant the page load did not show is not counted.
- **Schema v17** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php`): the new table `ab_exposures` has columns `pkey`, `test_id` (dictionary kind 18), `variant_id` (kind 19), `session_id`, `day`, `ts` and `clicks`. Its primary key is `(pkey, test_id)`, with keys `test_day (test_id, day, variant_id, session_id)` for results and `ts` for retention. Visitors and conversions per variant come from joining `session_id` to visits.
- **Retention** (`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-rollup.php`): rows are pruned with pageviews (visit retention). Uninstall and demo removal drop the table through `SEOProStats_Schema::names()`.
- **Opt-in one variant per visit** (`tracking_ab_visit`, Settings → Tracking, off by default). When off, each page load picks a variant again and nothing is stored, as in part 1. When on, the swap script (`SEOProStats_AB_Tests::script($visit)`) reads `sessionStorage` key `spst-ab-<test>` and keeps that variant if it is still offered (a control weighted 0 is not). Otherwise it picks by weight. It stores only the slug. The setting's description says that this is browser storage, which privacy law treats like cookies. The setting is one of the page cache's tracker settings, so changing it clears cached pages.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md` covers the hit fields, the browser-storage exception, the A/B tests section, and the tables and indexes. `README.md` and `readme.txt` cover user docs and the FAQ. `changelog.txt` and the README changelog are updated.

Visitor pages pay nothing new: no query, option write or remote request. The collector is unchanged; it already passes hit fields through.

## Verification

- `composer install && bash scripts/lint.sh`: **all passed** (php js shell workflows phpcs phpstan build; the webpack size warnings were already there).
- `npm run --silent check` (typecheck): passed. The pre-push repo-verify typecheck also passed.
- `bash scripts/smoke-test.sh` (Docker, WordPress latest / PHP 8.3): **passed**. The plugin makes 0 queries of its own on every visitor page, with default settings and with every feature on. Query checks were OK, and uninstall lists `wp_seoprostats_ab_exposures` among the tables it drops.
- Disposable site (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3, MariaDB 10.6), Chromium through Playwright, not logged in. The page had two running tests: Hero A/B 50/50, and CTA A(0)/B/C 50/50.
  - **Setting off, 30 page loads, one click in the Hero variant each.** Every pageview carried `ab` (30/30) and every click its pair (30/30), with nothing in `sessionStorage`. After `wp seoprostats process`, `ab_exposures` held 60 rows: Hero A 15 / B 15, and CTA B 16 / C 14, with no CTA A (weight 0). There were 30 clicks, each on the variant that was clicked. These counts exactly match what the browser showed. 0 rows lacked their pageview or had a different visit.
  - **Forged hit** (curl): unknown test, unknown variant, bad format, a second pair for the same test, and a click claiming a variant the page did not show. Only the first valid pair was stored, only the click in the shown variant was counted, and the dictionary has only the real tests and variants.
  - **Setting on, 6 tabs × 5 reloads.** Every tab kept its first variant on every reload. Storage held only `spst-ab-herotest01=<slug>` and `spst-ab-ctatest02=<slug>`.
  - **Stale storage.** A bogus slug, or a control weighted 0, seeded in `sessionStorage` was ignored: the script picked again by weight and overwrote it (12/12 loads). A valid stored variant was kept 12/12.
  - **Retention.** A back-dated exposure was counted by `prune_counts()` and deleted by `SEOProStats_Rollup::prune()`; current rows stayed.
  - Schema v17 installed with the keys above (`SHOW INDEX`). A per-test, per-variant query uses `test_day`.
- Not checked: how the new Settings → Tracking row looks. The settings screen is built from the schema, and the row follows the same pattern as `tracking_search` beside it. Its value saved and read back correctly.
- GitHub Actions do not run on this private repository (billing), so the checks above were run locally, as `AGENTS.md` asks.

Resolves #134

title: GH#142: Search → Backlinks from the pages that send visits
body:
## Summary

Backlinks without an outside service (parent #37). SEOProStats_Backlinks runs from the daily cron (20-second budget, live data, new setting Settings → Data → Check pages that send visitors for links, on by default): it reads Referral visits since its last run from sessions into a new links table (schema v18; one row per referring page, address as dict kind DICT_URL), opens the pages due with wp_safe_remote_get() (5 s, 3 redirects, 1 MB, a user agent naming the plugin and site) and keeps their absolute links to the site's hosts, one row per linked page with anchor text (or [alt]) and rel bits (nofollow, sponsored, ugc; at most 50 per page). Each page again after 7 days; one with no link only after another visit from it. A link missing on 2 checks in a row, or on a page answering 404/410, is lost; failed requests only mark the page checked. title: GH#144: Search Console sitemaps and URL Inspection
body:
## Summary

Google's own view of the site's indexing, from Search Console (parent #37). SEOProStats_Inspections runs from the hourly search import while Search Console is connected (20-second budget, own lock, live data; never on visitor pages or report requests). Once a day it reads the property's sitemaps (webmasters/v3 sitemaps.list; Google's deprecated indexed count is not kept); problems are errors, warnings, not downloaded for over 7 days, and the site's own sitemap index not submitted. Then it inspects pages with the URL Inspection API (searchconsole v1 urlInspection/index:inspect), within a new setting Settings → Data → Google URL inspections (default 200 a day, 0 to 2,000, Google's per-property limit, counted per Pacific day): the pages Indexation lists first, then pages with Google impressions, each again after 14 days. Address errors (400/404) are kept as tried and the run goes on; quota, permission and server errors stop it and are shown. New inspections table (schema v19, path_id primary key, codes for verdicts and states, coverage and canonicals in the dictionary; keys checked, verdict_checked, coverage_checked, flags). Four audit findings: robots_blocked, not_indexed (crawled, currently not indexed), google_canonical, rich_errors. A verdict change is the new change kind index_status on the timeline. Sitemap problems are the new queue kind sitemap. /indexation and /audit rows carry google; /indexation adds sitemaps and inspections. REST GET /inspections, wp seoprostats inspect [<page>] [--run] [--sitemaps], doctor shows the run, ability seoprostats/inspections, OpenAPI and core types. Dashboard: Search → Audit gains Google's index after Indexation (sitemaps, pages inspected with a verdict switch, daily cap and last run), a Google column in Indexation, the four findings; Plan lists sitemap items. Demo data: twelve pages inspected, one verdict change, three sitemaps. Uninstall and demo removal clean up.

title: GH#161: launch sweep, security: filter backslash escaping, inline reasons, pinned workflow, dev dependency fixes
body:
## What

Launch sweep, security area (parent #160).

- **Fixed (real bug, CodeQL `js/incomplete-sanitization`):** a filter value ending in a backslash ran into the next value. `serializeFilter()` wrote `a\` and `b` as `a\,b`, which both readers took as the one value `a,b`. Now `\\` is a backslash and `\,` a comma in a value; any other backslash is itself, so existing links read the same.
  - `packages/core/src/filters.ts`: escape `\` before `,`; `splitValues()` reads both escapes.
  - `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php`: new `split_values()` scan replaces the `(?<!\\),` lookbehind split, which had the same gap.
  - `docs/api/openapi.yaml`: the `filters` parameter documents `\\`.
- **Explained inline** (`STANDARDS.md` → Code): six `md5()` calls used as a cache key, fingerprint, ID or demo value (`// NOSONAR nosemgrep: <reason>`), and the Matomo import's `http://` address, only parsed for its path and query.
- **Workflow:** `.github/workflows/star-history.yml` (from the aidevops badge sync, not a starter core file) is pinned to the aidevops commit `repo-metrics.yml` uses (v3.38.4), with `contents: read` at the top and `write` on its job only.
- **Dependabot (development only):** `package.json` `overrides` move js-yaml 5, katex, postcss-selector-parser, serialize-javascript, smol-toml and uuid 8 to fixed versions. Their parents (`@wordpress/scripts`, `@wordpress/components`) pin below the fixes, so Dependabot cannot update them.
- `changelog.txt` gains the Unreleased section `README.md` already had, with PR #157's line.

Resolves #161

## Not changed, marked in the services after merge

False positives, each with the reason: loopback `http://` in `scripts/demo-site.sh` and `scripts/shop-test.sh`; `exec()` with every argument through `escapeshellarg()` in `scripts/replaced-plugins.php`; `collect.php`'s include path built from a digits-only value, and its HMAC echo; fixed-key jQuery selectors in `admin/js/seoprostats-admin.js`; the escaped glob in `packages/tracker/src/index.ts`; the literal regex in `Plan.tsx`; the same-origin REST URL in `api.ts`. Scorecard token-permission alerts for `release.yml` and `repo-metrics.yml`: those jobs must write.

Left open: `braces` 3.0.3 (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, every version, no fix published) is under `@wordpress/scripts`' file watchers. It is a build tool that expands only this repository's own patterns.

## Verification

- Round trip, both readers (disposable scripts): `["a\\","b"]`, `["x,y","z"]`, `["back\\slash","c\\,d","\\\\"]`, `["plain"]`, `[""]` serialize and parse back identically in TS and PHP; the old-style `a\b,c\,d` still reads as `["a\\b","c,d"]` in both.
- `npm run build` after the overrides: no file in `assets/build/` changes, CSS minification included.
- `npm audit`: the 7 Dependabot advisories are gone; only `braces` remains.
- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, js, shell, workflows, PHPCS, PHPStan level 7, build) passes; `npm run typecheck` passes; `scripts/sync-core.sh --check`: all 59 core files match the starter.

## Summary

Resolves #146. Imports backlink exports through Settings → Import → Links, multipart/JSON REST requests and WP-CLI, with resumable budgeted cron processing and source filtering in Search → Backlinks.

- Integration: existing API/CLI report patterns, Import tab and Backlinks dashboard.
- Exports without target URLs are candidates for verification, not fabricated links.

- Schema v20 keeps immutable discovery bits and per-provider scores and dates. Verification adds a separate page-check bit without falsely attributing targets to another export.

- Staging uses non-autoloaded 500-row chunks, capped at 100,000 rows/50 MB, with crash recovery, checkpointed progress and cleanup. No public uploads are retained.

## Decisions

- Ambiguous headers can be overridden in the Import card, REST `source`, or CLI `--source`.
- Exports are samples. Only safe referring-page verification establishes a loss, and re-importing cannot resurrect a verified loss.
- Source filtering applies before aggregation/paging within the existing indexed, bounded 5,000-row report window; this limit is documented rather than widening report query costs.

title: GH#50: Search Console Sign in with Google through a stateless relay
body:
## What

Sign in with Google for the Search Console connection, through a stateless relay we run (`relay/gsc-oauth`, a Cloudflare Worker for `gsc-oauth.wpallstars.com`, kept out of the zips by `.distignore`). The service-account key stays as the other way and is unchanged.

## How

- **Relay** (`relay/gsc-oauth/worker.mjs`): `/start` shows which site is asking, then sends the browser to Google's consent screen with HMAC-signed state (15 minutes). `/callback` exchanges the code and posts the tokens to the site in a self-submitting form, never in a URL. `/refresh` exchanges a refresh token for an access token. It stores nothing and observability is off.
- **Plugin** (`SEOProStats_Source_Search_Console`):
  - Adds a second credential type, `{type: google, refresh_token}`.
  - Keeps one-time nonces and finished sign-ins in a transient for 15 minutes.
  - Gets access tokens from the relay and keeps each one encrypted until 2 minutes before it expires. That works out to about one relay request per hour per site.
  - Revokes the token with Google on disconnect, and when a sign-in is replaced by a key or a new sign-in.
- **Connections tab**: shows **Sign in with Google** first, with the key steps under a details element. The return goes through admin-post (both priv and nopriv hooks, because a cross-site POST can arrive without cookies). The tab's script then finishes the connection; if it can't find the site's own property, it offers the account's properties.
- **REST**: `POST /connections/search-console` accepts `google: true`, and statuses gain `method`. The OpenAPI spec is updated to match.
- **Docs**: `readme.txt` External services (the relay), `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `todo/PLANS.md`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (php, js, shell, PHPCS, PHPStan level 8, build).
- Relay deployed to `https://gsc-oauth.wpallstars.com` (Worker `seoprostats-gsc-oauth`, secrets `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `STATE_KEY`). Home 200; a bad start link 400; a fake refresh token gets Google's `invalid_grant` (so the client credentials are accepted); the consent link has the `/callback` redirect, `webmasters.readonly` and `access_type=offline`.
- End to end on a local test site: Sign in with Google → consent → connected to `sc-domain:wpallstars.com` (the local site has no property, so it was picked from the account's), first import done (24 days, 213 rows, then continuing in the background).
- Refresh: the cached access token was deleted and `token()` got a new one through the relay `/refresh`, cached it again, and listed 43 properties with it.
- Not run: disconnect (revoking the test connection); revoke is a plain POST to Google's revoke endpoint.

Resolves #50

title: fix: a running import no longer brings back a disconnected search source
body:
## What

If you disconnect a search source while its import is running in WP-Cron, it now stays disconnected. Before, it came back.

This was reported while testing #181: the site disconnected, then immediately showed **Connected** with "HTTP 401: Request had invalid authentication credentials".

## Why

An import runs in its own request for up to about a minute. That request has its own cached copy of the `seoprostats_connections` option, because WordPress caches options per request. When the disconnect, in another request, deleted the option, the import kept going. The next `update_state()` read the stale cached copy, merged its progress into it, and wrote the whole thing back, credentials included. The token had just been revoked, so the next Google request returned 401. The same happens with a service-account key; the key just keeps working afterwards, so it went unnoticed.

## Fix

- `SEOProStats_Connections::all_fresh()` clears the option's cache entry and reads it again before every write (`save()`, `update_state()`, `remove()`).
- `still_connected()` checks the database. The import loops (days, Bing pages with their queries, search appearances) call it before each step, so a disconnect stops a running import before it writes more rows. Without this, a disconnect with "delete data" could get rows written again after the delete.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (PHPCS, PHPStan level 8, build).
- Reproduced on the preview site with `wp eval`: read the connections (now cached), delete the option behind WordPress's back the way another request would, then call `update_state()`. Results are in the comment below.

title: GH#147: Link spam review and Google disavow file export
body:
## Summary

Resolves #147.

Implement local explained backlink review, stored owner decisions, prior-list preservation and Google disavow text export. Nothing is submitted externally.

## Implementation

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-backlink-review.php`: explained weighted signals, domain/URL decisions, bounded indexed reads, strict validation and transactional prior-list merge.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-schema.php` and `class-seoprostats-backlinks.php`: schema v22, indexed InnoDB review storage and facts retained from existing page fetches, with no extra external requests.
- REST, WP-CLI and `seoprostats/backlink-review` share the same permission-checked implementation; HTTP downloads are plain-text attachments rather than JSON-wrapped strings.
- Dashboard, portable types, demo cases, OpenAPI, architecture, user guidance and committed build assets are included. Existing backlink reporting and WordPress components are the integration patterns.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk level: high — owner decisions and replacement-list export.
- Testing level: runtime-verified.
- Final implementation head: `0e5e91d`.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`, `npm run check`, `npm run build` and offline release preflight passed; generated dashboard assets match source.
- Smoke tests passed on WordPress 7.1.3/PHP 8.3 and minimum WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4, including indexed report queries and a large content fixture.
- Final-head disposable WordPress runtime verification passed on both runtimes: good/spam scores and reasons; observed page facts; weak supplied authority versus unknown authority; separate supplied spam scores; owner auditing; domain keep including subdomains; two domain entries plus one unchanged URL; prior-list preservation and idempotence; merge conflict rollback under READ COMMITTED; InnoDB storage; UTF-8, URL-length, line and byte limits; demo isolation; anonymous read/write denial; authenticated raw HTTP text export; ability execution where supported; failed database-read rejection; CLI and uninstall cleanup.
- Dashboard is built and typechecked; no browser-interaction or visual QA is claimed.

## Safety and trade-offs

- Signals are hints, not proof. Supplied low authority is only a five-point hint and never substituted for a spam score; missing evidence stays unknown. Keep decisions suppress future flags.
- Invalid input, failed reads, conflicting keep/undecided entries and oversized output fail without producing a partial replacement file.
- Most sites never need disavow. Upload manually only where Google recommends it, to a URL-prefix property; each upload replaces the old list. Bing's removed tool/API and other engines remain out of scope.
- Main's refactors were retained; the PR helper finalized the WIP history before the final fast-forward authority-signal commit. Existing webpack bundle-size warnings predate this task.

## Summary

Second part of #174. Splits the remaining long functions in `SEOProStats_Processor` (the batch processor that turns buffered hits into visits, pageviews, events, clicks and pages) into named private helpers. No public method, hook, REST route, WP-CLI command, SQL statement or stored data changes.

`includes/stats/class-seoprostats-processor.php`:

- `process()`: line and hit flattening (`flatten_line()`, `flatten_hit()`, `engagement()`, `is_fact()`) and the batch's dictionary texts (`batch_texts()`, `fact_texts()`).
- `visits()`: stored-visit lookup (`stored_visits()`), refunds (`refund_visit()`), joining or starting a visit (`join_visit()`) and adding a hit (`add_hit()`); the nested ternary is now an `if`/`elseif`.
- `fact()`: `props()`, `prop_text()` (the nested ternary), `revenue()`, `page_kind()`.
- `ab_known()` and `write_exposures()`: `variant_slugs()`, `exposure_rows()`.
- `write_sessions()`: `session_row()`.
- `write_facts()`: `write_pageviews()`, `pageview_prop_rows()`, `event_pages()`, `write_events()`.
- `write_pages()` and `page()`: `page_view()`, `stale_pages()`, `is_post_page()`, `page_taxonomy()`, `page_term()`.
- `split_url()`: `url_param()`.
- One chunked multi-row insert helper, `insert_rows()`, now used by exposures, pageviews, properties and clicks. It builds the same statements as before.
- `search_words()`: the character class no longer repeats what `\s` already matches (`\x09`–`\x0D`). It matches the same characters.

title: GH#213: backlink import history, reported pages and catch-up checks
body:
## Summary

A Search Console "Linking pages" export names the page linking, not the page it links to. Importing 883 of them on a live site gave `accepted: 880` but Search → Backlinks stayed at zero: the rows are referring-page candidates (`path_id=0`) that only become links once the check opens each page, and the daily 20-second check would have taken weeks. Nothing in the UI said so, and there was no record of what was imported.

### Reported pages (Search → Backlinks)

- New `reported` list and tile: every referring page an export named, with its check state (`unchecked`, `links`, `none`, `error`, `gone`), live links found on it, the export's date and the last check. Source filter (`found=`) now lives in the URL, so other screens can link to one source's results.
- `SEOProStats_Backlinks_Reported` reads the `path_id=0` range of the `path_checked` key (at most 5,000 rows, never-checked first).
- Totals gain `reported`, `reported_domains`, `reported_checked`; `read.next` gives the catch-up's next run.
- A failed open now counts in the page row's `misses` (reset on success), so `error` is distinguishable from `none`.

### Catch-up check

- When an import ends, and after every run, cron `seoprostats_backlinks_check` is scheduled a minute ahead while the check is on and an export-named page was never opened. It reschedules itself until none waits.
- The daily run, the catch-up, **Check now** (`POST /backlinks/check`, admins, live data) and `wp seoprostats backlinks check` share a five-minute option lease (`run_locked()`), so pages are never opened twice at once.
- Links found on an exported page's first check are dated from the export and raise no `backlink_new` change: the export already said they existed.

### Import history (Settings → Import → Links)

- `SEOProStats_Backlinks_History`: the last 20 imports (who, how, file name/size/SHA-256, source, rows, status), in one non-autoloaded option per data set.
- Uploaded and CLI files are copied to `wp-content/seoprostats/links-{blog}/` under random names, with deny-all `.htaccess` and `index.php`. At most 200 MB of files are kept, oldest dropped first.
- Table with a **Download** button (`GET /backlinks/imports/{id}/file`, admins, `no-store`, `nosniff`, served raw via `rest_pre_serve_request`) and a link to Search → Backlinks → Reported for that source.
- `GET /backlinks/imports`, `wp seoprostats backlinks imports|reported`, and the `seoprostats/backlinks` ability's `reported` kind and `source` input.
- The card's status reads in words, and the page reloads into the history when an import finishes.
- Reset and uninstall remove entries, files and folder (`SEOProStats_Backlinks::reset()`).

### Docs

`docs/api/openapi.yaml` (new routes and schemas), `docs/architecture.md`, `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).

## Privacy and performance

- Visitor pages unchanged: no new query, option write or remote request.
- New queries use existing keys (`path_checked`).
- Downloads are limited to administrators and served from a folder that denies direct access.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan shell`: pass. `scripts/lint.sh build`: committed build matches a fresh build. `npm run check` (tsc): pass.
- Runtime results (smoke test, demo-site import of the two CSVs) are posted as a comment below.

Resolves #213

title: GH#215: period presets in whole weeks (last 28, 91, 182, 364 days)
body:
## What

New period presets in whole weeks: **Last 28 days** (`28d`), **Last 91 days** (`91d`), **Last 182 days** (`182d`) and **Last 364 days** (`364d`). The existing presets stay.

On Search, a whole-week period (these four and Last 7 days) keeps its length and ends on the newest day with search data (`through`), as Search Console's own periods do. Other periods are still cut at `through`, as before.

## Why

"Previous period" takes the same number of whole days just before the range (`SEOProStats_Query::compare_range()`). With 30 or 90 days the two periods start on different weekdays, so weekends meet weekdays and the change figures are skewed. With a multiple of 7, each day meets the same weekday.

Search cut the period at `through` (about 3–4 days back) and compared the cut length. So "Last 28 days" would have become 24 days compared with 24 days, starting on different weekdays. Keeping the length fixes that.

## How

- `packages/core/src/types.ts`: `RANGE_KEYS` gets the four keys, ordered by length among the day ranges. The period menu follows this order.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/labels.ts`: their labels.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php`: `RANGES` gets the four keys. New `DAY_RANGES` feeds `range()`, and `day_range()`'s existing `(int) $key` path resolves the keys. New `WEEK_RANGES` lists the whole-week keys. REST, WP-CLI and abilities take their enum from `RANGES`, so all three accept the new keys.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` `days()`: for `WEEK_RANGES`, the first day is `through` minus the range's length. Rankings, Opportunities, Content, Audit, Targets, Links, Coverage and the loop all go through `days()`, so they agree.
- Docs: `docs/api/openapi.yaml` (enum and description), `docs/architecture.md` (Ranges, Search), WP-CLI `--range` help, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`.
- `assets/build/` rebuilt.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan and build all pass. The build is up to date, and the pre-push typecheck passes.
- I called the real `SEOProStats_Query::range()`/`compare_range()` and `SEOProStats_Search::days()` from a throwaway script that stands in for WordPress (site time zone Europe/London, today 10 Oct 2026, search data through 6 Oct). The 30d Google row matches the dashboard screenshot in the issue (11 Sept – 6 Oct vs 16 Aug – 10 Sept).

title: GH#214: dark mode for the plugin screens, loading placeholders for light and dark
body:
## What

**Dark mode for SEO Pro Stats' screens** (Statistics and Settings), and **loading placeholders that work in light and dark**, in wp-admin and in shared reports.

- A sun, moon or half-circle icon button to the right of **Buy me a coffee** opens a menu: **Light** (the default, WordPress's own colours), **Dark**, or **System** (follows the computer's light or dark setting, live).
- Each person chooses for themselves. The choice is user meta (`seoprostats_admin_theme`), as WordPress keeps the admin colour scheme, so it follows them to any browser.
- The rest of wp-admin, the Dashboard widget and the post editor keep WordPress's colours.
- Loading placeholders are drawn from the text colour, so they read on any surface. A loading table shows a header and rows; the main chart shows faint grid lines and a soft area at its final height.

## Why

The fixed light-grey placeholders were close to invisible on a shared report in dark mode, and wp-admin had no dark option. The WordPress.org admin dark-mode plugins the owner pointed to apply site-wide and repaint every screen. This keeps WordPress first: light is untouched WordPress, dark is WordPress's own admin greys, and only our screens change.

## How

- `includes/admin/class-seoprostats-admin-theme.php` (new): the mode (`light|dark|system`, default `light`), the admin-ajax save (nonce, `read` capability, allow-list), styles and script loaded only on the plugin's two screen hooks, and a few lines first in `<head>` that set `spst-theme-{mode}` and `spst-dark` on `<html>` before first paint, so nothing flashes.
- `admin/js/seoprostats-theme.js` (new): the button and a `menuitemradio` menu (arrows, Home, End, Escape, focus return, a tick on the current mode, `wp.a11y.speak` on change). It follows `prefers-color-scheme` while System is chosen, saves, and on failure goes back to the previous mode and says so. It fires `spst-themechange`.
- `admin/css/seoprostats-theme.css` (new): one palette (`--spst-ui-*`, WordPress admin greys). The plugin's tokens and WordPress components' `--wp-components-color-*` read it. Classic admin elements on these screens (fields, buttons, notices, tables, Screen Options) get it through low-specificity `:where()` rules, so WordPress's focus styles and any class rule still win. Primary buttons keep the admin colour scheme's fill; accent text uses `color-mix(accent 55%, #fff)` (fallback `#72aee6`). Colours ease for 0.2 s between modes, never on load, and not with reduced motion.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/common.css`, `dashboard.css`, `share.css`: the placeholders (`currentColor` mixes, a masked table and chart, one slow sweep, still with reduced motion). Fixed colours became tokens, and in dark, shared reports' tooltips and change markers use the same lighter colours.
- `packages/wp-admin/src/components/MainChart.tsx`, `Overview.tsx`, `Search.tsx`: the chart reads its colours from the tokens and redraws on `spst-themechange`; the chart placeholder.
- `includes/class-seoprostats-setup.php` loads it; `uninstall.php` removes the user meta.

title: GH#220: default to Last 91 days; Search keeps the full length of every Last N period
body:
## What

1. **The dashboard opens on Last 91 days** instead of Last 30 days, so the default comparison meets the same weekdays. A new shared report without a range defaults to the same. Links and bookmarks that name a period keep it.
2. **On Search, every period counted back from today keeps its length**, ending on the newest day with search data (`through`). Before, only the whole-week periods did (#217). This now covers Last 30 days, Last 90 days and Last 12 months: Last 30 days holds 30 days instead of 26. This week, month and year, today and yesterday are still cut at `through`.

## How

- `packages/core/src/state.ts`: `DEFAULT_STATE.range` is `91d`. The hash leaves out the default, so a hash without `range` now opens on 91 days.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-shares.php`: `view()`'s range fallback is `91d`. Saved shares always store their range, so existing shares don't change.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-query.php`: `WEEK_RANGES` is replaced by `TRAILING_RANGES` (`7d`, `28d`, `30d`, `90d`, `91d`, `182d`, `364d`, `12mo`).
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-search.php` `days()`: uses `TRAILING_RANGES`. Rankings, Opportunities, Content, Audit, Targets, Links, Coverage and the loop all go through it.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (Search, Ranges), `README.md`, `changelog.txt` (new Unreleased section after 1.3.0).
- `assets/build/` rebuilt. `editor.js` changes too: it imports `DEFAULT_STATE`, and its link names `range=90d` explicitly now.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan and build all pass; the pre-push typecheck passes.
- I ran the real `parseHash()`/`buildHash()` from `packages/core/src/state.ts`, bundled with esbuild:

```
""                                   → 91d prev → rebuilt: #/overview
"#/search"                           → 91d prev → rebuilt: #/search
"#/overview?range=30d"               → 30d prev → rebuilt: #/overview?range=30d
"#/overview?range=7d&compare=year"   → 7d year → rebuilt: #/overview?range=7d&compare=year
```

- I called the real `SEOProStats_Query::range()`/`compare_range()` and `SEOProStats_Search::days()` from a throwaway script that stands in for WordPress (today 10 Oct 2026, search data through 6 Oct). Before this change, 30d gave 11 Sept – 6 Oct (26 days):

```
Google (daily)
  30d    30 days Mon 2026-09-07 – 2026-10-06  vs   30 days Sat 2026-08-08 – 2026-09-06
  90d    90 days Thu 2026-07-09 – 2026-10-06  vs   90 days Fri 2026-04-10 – 2026-07-08
  91d    91 days Wed 2026-07-08 – 2026-10-06  vs   91 days Wed 2026-04-08 – 2026-07-07
  12mo  365 days Tue 2025-10-07 – 2026-10-06  vs  365 days Mon 2024-10-07 – 2025-10-06
  week    2 days Mon 2026-10-05 – 2026-10-06  (still cut)
  month   6 days Thu 2026-10-01 – 2026-10-06  (still cut)
Bing (weekly): 30d is 35 days, the five whole weeks holding the 30 days; 90d is 91.
```

title: GH#224: links import never waits for good; tab keeps reading progress; reported label
body:
Resolves #224

## Summary

A links import on a live site stayed at "Importing: 0 of 883 rows", then showed "The response is not a valid JSON response." The plugin's files were being replaced by an update two minutes after the upload. The import's cron event was used up without running, and one status poll got WordPress's critical-error page. Nothing restarts a running import, and the tab stopped polling on its first error. Details and evidence: #224.

- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-api.php` `backlinks_import_status()`: while the job runs, each poll calls `SEOProStats_Backlinks_Import::run(POLL_BUDGET)` (4 s, under the existing lease; `run()` reschedules the cron event). An administrator watching the tab sees progress without cron. Admin-only route: visitor pages are untouched.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-collection.php` `backlinks_import_due()` (hourly): reschedules a running import that has no event.
- `admin/js/seoprostats-import.js`: "Uploading and reading the file…" with an indeterminate bar while the file is sent, polls every 1.5 s, retries a failed poll with backoff (5 to 30 s, 10 times) instead of stopping, and checks the status before reporting a failed upload (the site may have kept the file).
- `packages/wp-admin/src/Backlinks.tsx`: reported state `none` reads "Visit the link to check for backlinks", as the owner asked. The check cannot see links added by scripts or hidden from automated visits.
- `includes/stats/class-seoprostats-changes.php` `deleted_plugin()`: ignores the plugin's own deletion. Deleting it while loaded (`delete_plugins()` from WP-CLI eval) fataled on a lazy `require_once` after its files were gone.

## Verification

Disposable WordPress (PHP 8.3, `DISABLE_WP_CRON`, nothing runs `wp-cron.php`), zip built from this branch, the real 883-row export:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Browser: Settings → Import upload; first progress check answered with a 503 HTML page | "Importing: 0 of 883" → "Still importing, but the progress could not be read just now. Trying again in 5 seconds." → "Importing: 499 of 883" → "Last import done: 880 rows kept, 3 skipped."; tab reloaded with the history row (Done, Download, results link); 16 s, 3 polls |
| REST upload, then status polls only (no cron) | first poll: done, 880 kept, 3 skipped |
| Lost event: upload, `cron event delete`, run `seoprostats_hourly` | event=no → event=yes → after its run: done |
| `delete_plugins()` with the plugin loaded | ok, folder gone, no fatal |
| `debug.log` | empty throughout |
| `scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan build` | pass |

title: GH#231: edit links for custom post types without a base and for term archives
body:
Resolves #231

## What

Page rows (Search → Rankings → Pages, Clicks, Opportunities, Content, Targets, Plan and the rest: all go through `SEOProStats_Clicks::page_info()`) showed "View page" without "Edit" when `url_to_postid()` could not find the post.

- **Custom post types without a base.** When a plugin or theme removes a custom post type's base (`/my-entry/` instead of `/type/my-entry/`), `url_to_postid()` matches the path against the `post` rewrite rule and finds nothing, because the base removal usually applies only to the main query. Now, when `url_to_postid()` returns 0, the path's last part is looked up among published posts of viewable post types (indexed `post_name`) and kept only when that post's own permalink has the same path.
- **Term archives** (category, tag and custom taxonomy pages) are not posts, so they never had an editor link. A path that is no post is now looked up among terms of viewable taxonomies (indexed `slug`), kept only when the term link has the same path, and carries `term_id` and `taxonomy`. `with_edit_url()` links to the term's edit screen with `edit_term`.

Lookups stay inside the report cache; edit permission is still checked on every request. Docs: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `packages/core/src/types.ts`, `changelog.txt`.

## Decisions

- A candidate is accepted only when its own permalink (or term link) has the path, so a same-slug post of another type, or a draft, never gets the link.
- Term identity is added as optional `term_id` / `taxonomy` fields instead of reusing `post_id`.
